title: ～かぎり — “as long as ～ / as far as ～”
summary: Sets a limit or range: “as long as the condition holds” or “within what I know/can do.” It attaches to the plain form of a verb or adjective (な-adj + な / である, noun + の). The main clause is usually a stable result.

patterns.form: 動詞・形容詞 普通形＋かぎり
知る・見る・聞く など＋かぎり
patterns.gloss: as far as I know / see / hear

body.p: A かぎり B means B holds while A continues. 体が動くかぎり、この仕事を続けたい: as long as my body moves. The negative ～ないかぎり means “unless” (努力しないかぎり、上達しない).
With verbs of perception or knowledge, かぎり limits the range: 私が知っているかぎり、彼は嘘をつく人ではない. The speaker is only speaking from their own information.

Verbs and い-adjectives use the plain form (勉強しているかぎり). な-adjectives use な (元気なかぎり) and nouns use の (学生であるかぎり). The main clause is not an order or request that depends on the speaker’s will at the same moment.

examples.ja: 毎日（まいにち）これだけ 勉強（べんきょう）している かぎり、心配（しんぱい）ない。
examples.romaji: Mainichi kore dake benkyou shite iru kagiri, shinpai nai.
examples.tr: As long as you study this much every day, there is nothing to worry about.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）が知（し）っているかぎり、彼（かれ）はうそをつく人（ひと）ではない。
examples.romaji: Watashi ga shitte iru kagiri, kare wa uso o tsuku hito dewa nai.
examples.tr: As far as I know, he isn’t someone who tells lies.

examples.ja: 体（からだ）が動（うご）くかぎり、この仕事（しごと）を続（つづ）けたい。
examples.romaji: Karada ga ugoku kagiri, kono shigoto o tsudzuketai.
examples.tr: As long as my body can move, I want to keep this job.

pitfalls: ～ないかぎり means “unless”, not “as long as … not”. Both readings are connected, but translate it as “unless”.
Do not confuse かぎり with だけ or ばかり. かぎり marks a limit of time or range.
